name: Greenfield: click analytics for shortened URLs
requirement: Add click analytics for shortened URLs.
whyThisType: The baseline URL shortener had no analytics at all: no table, no entity, no endpoint. The increment adds a new capability rather than changing existing behaviour.
expectedOrchestrationBehaviour: Requirement is unambiguous, so the clarification gate does not trigger.
requirement-analysis -> codebase-analysis -> planning -> architecture run sequentially.
PRE_IMPLEMENTATION approval gate blocks the implementation task until a human approves.
tests, security and documentation run in parallel after implementation.
validation joins the three parallel branches.
FINAL approval gate blocks the transition to COMPLETED.
validationExpectations: A successful redirect records exactly one click event.
Unknown (404), disabled (410) and expired (410) redirects record nothing.
Analytics are read back from the database, not from an in-memory counter.
All pre-existing URL shortener behaviour still passes.

tests: url-shortener-service: ShortUrlServiceTest (click recorded / not recorded, analytics delegation)
url-shortener-service: ShortUrlApiIntegrationTest (baseline behaviour unchanged, analytics path published in OpenAPI)

intentionalBoundaries: No IP address, user agent, device fingerprint or geo-location is stored - only the click time and the optional Referer.
No dashboard, no aggregation service, no time-series store.
The recent-clicks window is capped at 10 entries.
Existing shortener migrations are untouched; the feature ships as a new Flyway migration.
